Subject: Children’s ibuprofen recall: affected lots, syringe error and what to do

Parents, we know this recall is frightening, especially if you have already given your child a dose. Here is what is affected, what went wrong and what to do now.

WHICH PRODUCT?

Corvane Pediatric Ibuprofen Oral Suspension 100 mg/5 mL, berry flavour, 120 mL bottle.

Affected lots: CV6114A and CV6114B
Expiry: 08/2027

If you have a Corvane bottle at home, check the lot number on the bottom of the box first. If you no longer have the box or cannot find the lot, bring the bottle to a pharmacist for help identifying it. Do not use the supplied syringe while you are unsure.

WHAT WENT WRONG?

The supplied syringe has incorrectly printed volume markings. Each labelled mark measures twice the volume shown:
• The mark labelled 2.5 mL actually measures 5 mL.
• The mark labelled 5 mL actually measures 10 mL.

Using these markings gives approximately twice the intended dose.

According to Corvane’s recall notice, the liquid medicine itself meets specifications and is not contaminated. These lots are not expired. The problem is the syringe, but that error can cause an overdose and needs to be taken seriously.

WHAT SHOULD PARENTS DO?

Stop using the syringe supplied with either affected lot and discard it. Do not try to compensate by using a different mark on the faulty syringe. Use only a correctly marked oral syringe, with the appropriate dose confirmed by a pharmacist or clinician.

If you used the affected syringe, think too much may have been given, or have any doubt about a dose already given, call the Ontario Poison Centre at 1-844-764-7669 (1-844-POISON-X). It is available 24 hours a day. Do not wait for symptoms or a Facebook reply.

Have the bottle, your child’s weight, and the amounts and times of doses ready if possible. Risk depends on the child’s weight, how much was given, how many doses were given and health factors, including kidney problems. We cannot assess an individual child safely through Facebook.

If an incorrect dose may have been given, do not give another dose of ibuprofen until the poison centre or your child’s doctor says it is safe.

If your child is very sleepy, hard to wake, vomiting blood, not urinating or having a seizure, seek emergency care immediately—call 911 or go to the emergency department.

REPLACEMENTS AND REFUNDS

Free replacement syringes are expected Monday, November 9, before noon. No receipt is needed, and they are available to anyone who needs one. You can also return affected product for a full refund. We will have extra opening hours Saturday, 10 a.m.–4 p.m., for exchanges.

Please share this information so families can check their supplies.

Rania, pharmacist
Cedarbrook Pharmacy
